passages.text:
When the blossoms fall the fruit appears,
When the former vanish the fruit is tasted. Till bread is broken, how can it serve as food?
Till the grapes are crushed, how can they yield wine? Till citrons be pounded up with drugs,
How can they afford healing to the sick?
passages.note: Being broken as part of growth and transformation

passages.text:
A friend is needed; travel not the road alone,
Take not thy own way through this desert!
passages.note: Loneliness; needing companions on a hard road

passages.text:
But if thou takest umbrage at every rub,
How wilt thou become a polished mirror?"
passages.note: Taking offence easily; friction that refines us

passages.text:
Whoso recognizes and confesses his own defects
Is hastening in the way that leads to perfection! But he advances not towards the Almighty
Who fancies himself to be perfect. No sickness worse than fancying thyself perfect
Can infect thy soul, O arrogant misguided one!
passages.note: Admitting flaws; the danger of thinking oneself perfect

passages.text:
If you desire to rise above mere names and letters,
Make yourself free from self at one stroke! Like a sword be without trace of soft iron;
Like a steel mirror, scour off all rust with contrition; Make yourself pure from all attributes of self,
That you may see your own pure bright essence!
passages.note: Letting go of ego to find one's true self
